signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Holds ~$60 but into a hawkish Fed and toppy positioning
signals.detail: Silver ~$60 (Thu 23 Jul, ~flat, +~130% YTD); gold -2% to ~$4,060 on real yields
signals.takeaway: The single most important line item for this book and its highest-beta pain. Silver held ~$60 on the war/inflation-hedge bid and copper-led industrial strength, but BofA flags a gold 'death cross', elevated net-longs and worst-quarter-in-13-years risk, and gold's ~2% real-yield-driven drop to ~$4,060 is the warning. The metal is trading as a rate/geopolitical asset into the 28-29 Jul FOMC (~83% hold, no cut, live hike tail). Structural deficit thesis holds (Silver Institute; JPMorgan ~$81 avg), but treat the rebound as a spot to right-size leverage/harvest into the Fed, not to add; $58 is the near-term line to hold.

signals.name: Crude oil / Energy
signals.label: Brent tops $100 on Houthi tanker strikes — Goldman flags $120 risk
signals.detail: Brent ~$100 (+6-7%), WTI ~$90 (+5%) on 23 Jul as the ceasefire collapsed
signals.takeaway: The Hormuz war premium is the dominant cross-portfolio driver this run: bullish the energy sleeve and Seatrium's offshore-order backdrop and a safe-haven bid for metals, but the same oil spike revives the inflation impulse that keeps the Fed and MAS hawkish — a headwind for HK tech, S-REITs and levered silver. Goldman warns $120 if Hormuz stays disrupted. Trade the de-escalation risk, not the individual legs; a ceasefire would reverse the oil/metals bid and relieve the rate premium.

signals.name: US mega-cap tech
signals.label: Melt-up cracks — Alphabet -7%, Tesla -14% lead a -2.2% Nasdaq day
signals.detail: S&P -1.2% to 7,408, Nasdaq -2.2% to 25,138 on 23 Jul; 10Y year-high ~4.62%
signals.takeaway: The oil/yield shock cracked the record run, led by mega-cap AI (Alphabet -7% on capex worry, Tesla -14% on earnings) as yields hit year-highs — a negative read-through for HK-tech beta (SMIC, the Tencent book) and rate-sensitive S-REITs. But credit is calm (HY ~268bp) and longer-term breadth broad (~69% >200-DMA), so this looks like a sharp oil/rate narrowing, not a break. Whether the 29 Jul FOMC and this week's mega-cap earnings deepen or resolve it is the swing.

signals.name: Rare earths (ex-China basket)
signals.label: China entity bans + MP's $110/kg DoD floor keep the ex-China thesis structurally bid
signals.detail: China's dual-use export ban on MP/USAR under active July enforcement; IEA: $6.5T at risk
signals.takeaway: The China/US rare-earth decoupling structurally favors the ex-China watchlist (Lynas — not targeted, advancing a US magnet MOU with Noveon; Energy Fuels; Iluka) and JL MAG's China-magnet position. MP's ~15% DoD stake with a $110/kg NdPr price floor plus Apple's $500M partnership de-risk the whole Western complex. The 10 Nov control-suspension expiry is the key catalyst — a dip on China-retaliation headlines is a watchlist entry to accumulate on weakness, not chase.

signals.name: Singapore blue-chips / S-REITs
signals.label: Q2 GDP +5.7% beats, but core CPI to 1.6% raises hawkish-MAS REIT risk
signals.detail: SG Q2 GDP +5.7% y/y; core CPI 1.6%; MAS review end-July; Singtel S$2B buyback
signals.takeaway: A resilient domestic economy supports DBS credit quality and the property/consumer names (UOL, CityDev, VICOM) into early-August earnings, and Singtel's S$2B buyback is a structural bid under a core holding. But accelerating core inflation (1.6%) plus the oil spike raise the odds of a hawkish-MAS tilt (stronger SGD, higher-for-longer) that pressures the S-REIT sleeve (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PAC, CapLand China Trust) — the end-July MPS is the near-term catalyst.

signals.name: Tencent / HK tech
signals.label: Hunyuan-3 AI traction + HK$5bn buybacks vs Xiaomi layoffs — favor Tencent
signals.detail: Tencent scaled compute after Hy3 overload; HK$5.01B early-July buybacks; Xiaomi cutting jobs
signals.takeaway: Genuine AI-product traction (Hunyuan-3 demand overload, ~90% agent-task success) plus aggressive buybacks underpin the Tencent thesis — the core HK-tech position to hold through China-tech volatility. Xiaomi's layoffs on a sharp profit decline make it the weakest link in the trio; SMIC's 5nm pilot runs are a structural domestic-fab tailwind. Favor Tencent on relative strength, but the 23 Jul US risk-off and hawkish Fed are near-term headwinds for HK-tech beta.

signals.name: US Treasuries / rates
signals.label: Fed 28-29 Jul: ~83% hold, no cut, hike tail; yields at year-highs
signals.takeaway: The dominant macro headwind for the book's highest-beta pain (levered silver, gold miners) and for S-REITs stays higher-for-longer, with the oil spike pushing yields to year-highs and keeping a live hike tail. Chair Warsh's data-dependent, no-guidance regime removes the cushion of forward-guided cuts. The big USD cash pile earns ~3.5-3.75% as productive dry powder for a post-FOMC metals shakeout; a dovish 29 Jul surprise is the upside catalyst.

congress.rationale: The Michigan Democrat added Freddie Mac (traded 14 Jul, filed 23 Jul) amid renewed GSE-privatization chatter around Fannie/Freddie.
congress.deepDive: A fresh, timely filing (9-day lag) in a name that trades directly on the on-again/off-again Trump-administration push to release the GSEs from conservatorship — a policy-sensitive bet by a member on the Energy & Commerce committee.

congress.rationale: Trimmed Teledyne — the largest of a large basket of Armstrong trades all dated 27 Mar but filed 21 Jul, well past the STOCK Act 45-day window.
congress.deepDive: A newly-active filer disclosed a diversified basket (buys in STX, SNDK, SCHW, PYPL, DGX, PEP, RMD, UDR, POOL, PTC; sells in TDY and PNC) months late — Unusual Whales flagged the late filing as a STOCK Act violation. The pattern (add memory/storage + brokerage, trim defense-electronics and a regional bank) is a modest cyclical tilt.

congress.rationale: Reduced PNC Financial (traded 27 Mar, filed 21 Jul) — a regional-bank trim inside the same late-filed basket.
congress.deepDive: Paired against buys in Schwab and memory names, the PNC sell reads as a rotation within financials rather than a broad de-risk; notable mainly for the multi-month filing delay.

congress.rationale: Added Seagate (traded 27 Mar, filed 21 Jul) — a storage/memory-cycle bet alongside a SanDisk (SNDK) buy.
congress.deepDive: The memory/storage adds line up with the 2026 AI-storage upcycle that also lifted SanDisk and Micron; small size but on-theme with the AI-infrastructure trade.

congress.rationale: Bought SanDisk in the same 27 Mar (filed 21 Jul) basket — a memory play into the AI-storage cycle.
congress.deepDive: SanDisk was among the memory names that surged in the July semis run before the 23 Jul tech selloff; a small on-theme add by the member.

congress.rationale: The Kansas Republican senator bought Berkshire Hathaway B shares (traded 23 Jun, filed 21 Jul), pairing it with an Alphabet add.
congress.deepDive: A conservative blue-chip pairing (Berkshire + Alphabet) from a senator — notable as it echoes Berkshire's own GOOGL build under Greg Abel; a low-turnover, quality tilt.

congress.rationale: Added Alphabet (traded 23 Jun, filed 21 Jul) alongside a Berkshire buy.
congress.deepDive: The Alphabet add lands just before the stock's -7% AI-capex-driven drop on 23 Jul — timely on entry, now underwater; a widely-owned name across both Congress and super-investors.

congress.rationale: The Alabama senator exited American Water Works (traded 8 Jun, filed 16 Jul), pairing it with a Lockheed trim.
congress.deepDive: Tuberville, among Congress's most active traders, cut a defensive utility and a defense prime in the same window — a modest de-risk from rate-sensitive and geopolitically-exposed names.

congress.rationale: Trimmed Lockheed Martin (traded 8 Jun, filed 16 Jul) despite the escalating Middle-East conflict.
congress.deepDive: A contrarian defense trim into a hot geopolitical backdrop — either profit-taking after a defense run or a rotation call; notable given the member's high trading frequency.

congress.rationale: The Rhode Island Democrat trimmed Nvidia (up to ~$250K, also traded AAPL and MU) at elevated AI valuations.
congress.deepDive: A sizeable Nvidia sell that pre-dates the 23 Jul AI-capex selloff — a well-timed trim of the market's most-owned AI name by a senator, echoing Burry's chip-short thesis and Meuser's earlier staggered NVDA sells.

congress.rationale: The Louisiana Democrat bought Nvidia (up to ~$45K) on AI/chip momentum — the opposite side of Whitehouse's trim.
congress.deepDive: The split NVDA views across members (Fields buying, Whitehouse and Meuser selling) capture the market's own AI-capex debate now playing out in the 23 Jul tech drawdown.

congress.rationale: Added Charles Schwab (traded 27 Mar, filed 21 Jul) — a brokerage/financials tilt in the late-filed basket.
congress.deepDive: Schwab benefits from higher-for-longer rates on client cash sweeps; a small on-theme financials add paired against the PNC trim.

congress.rationale: Bought PayPal (traded 27 Mar, filed 21 Jul) — a fintech value add in the same basket.
congress.deepDive: PayPal has also appeared in Michael Burry's Q1 book — a fintech-value name showing up across both congressional and hedge-fund disclosures.

superInvestors.name: Scion Asset Management
superInvestors.rationale: Michael Burry disclosed a direct short on Micron (entry ~$1,051.87) on 2 July, on top of fresh 30 June shorts against NVIDIA, Applied Materials and SOXX, calling chips due a ~30% correction; in early July he trimmed his Palantir short after PLTR jumped ~9% on an Nvidia partnership.
superInvestors.deepDive: Having wound down Scion's SEC registration in late 2025, Burry now discloses via Substack rather than 13Fs — these are his freshest, most public bets and they worked into the 23 Jul selloff. He calls Micron 'cyclical like no other' (34 drawdowns >30% in 42 years); the trade is the cleanest smart-money expression of the AI-capex-peak thesis now visible in the tape.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.rationale: Berkshire fully exited UnitedHealth after a ~45% rebound — a fast contrarian in-and-out — while Barron's estimates ~$5-11B of Q2 buybacks (inferred from Buffett donation filings) against a record ~$397B cash pile.
superInvestors.deepDive: Under Greg Abel, Berkshire tripled Alphabet (+204%) and added new Delta, Alphabet-C and NY Times stakes in Q1 while trimming Chevron and BofA. The UNH exit after the rebound and an accelerating buyback (after ending a 21-month pause) signal Abel is willing to trade actively; Buffett said the 2026 pullback 'wasn't big enough' to deploy the cash. Q2 13F due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.name: Pershing Square
superInvestors.rationale: Bill Ackman raised Pershing's Howard Hughes stake to ~46.9% via a ~$900M transaction (13D/A filed), continuing to build a 'modern Berkshire'; he also signaled four new undisclosed equity positions to be revealed in the Q2 report.
superInvestors.deepDive: Ackman added Microsoft (~$2.09B, ~15%) and lifted Amazon while cutting Alphabet ~95% in Q1. The HHH build is the core of his holding-company vision; the four teased positions make his 14 Aug 13F one of the most-watched of the cycle.

superInvestors.name: Appaloosa
superInvestors.rationale: David Tepper nearly doubled Amazon (+98%) to make it his top holding at ~15.2% of the book, alongside adds in TSM and SanDisk.
superInvestors.deepDive: Tepper's Amazon conviction makes it the single most-consensus mega-cap long across the tracked whales (also top for Ackman and near-top for Tiger/Coleman) — a crowded position now exposed to the 23 Jul growth selloff. Q2 refresh due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.name: Duquesne Family Office
superInvestors.rationale: Stanley Druckenmiller exited Alphabet entirely and opened a new Broadcom stake while adding SanDisk, Seagate and Micron across 31 new positions and 23 exits; top holding is Natera (~18%).
superInvestors.deepDive: High-turnover repositioning ($3.4B / 68 positions) that leans into AI-storage/semis (AVGO/SNDK/STX/MU) while dropping GOOGL — a sharp contrast with Berkshire's Alphabet build and a mixed read on the AI trade heading into the semis wobble.

superInvestors.name: Tiger Global
superInvestors.rationale: Chase Coleman added TSM (+49%), Applied Materials (+85%), Broadcom (+25%), Meta (+12%) and Nvidia; top holdings GOOGL (~$4.2B), NVDA (~$2.8B), AMZN (~$2.6B).
superInvestors.deepDive: Tiger leaned harder into the AI-semis supply chain in Q1 — a stance now tested by the 23 Jul Alphabet/Tesla-led drawdown and Burry's chip shorts. The fund posted July gains but trailed rival Tiger cubs.

superInvestors.name: Soros Fund Management
superInvestors.rationale: George Soros's fund held an S&P 500 put as its top position ($773M) and added NVDA, TSM and EA while cutting Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft — a hedged, cautious posture.
superInvestors.deepDive: The large index-put top holding is a portfolio hedge rather than a directional short, but it captures the defensive tilt among some whales into a stretched tape — vindicated on the 23 Jul selloff. New Linde and BlackLine positions added.

superInvestors.name: Gates Foundation Trust
superInvestors.rationale: The Gates Foundation Trust held 22 concentrated positions (~$31.7B) with no notable individual changes surfacing this cycle — a low-turnover, blue-chip book (Microsoft, Berkshire, Waste Management, Canadian National).
superInvestors.deepDive: Included as a stable long-horizon reference book; its concentration and inactivity contrast with the high-turnover hedge funds and make it a useful 'permanent capital' benchmark. Q2 13F due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.name: Trump / Trump Media (DJT)
superInvestors.rationale: Forbes pegs Trump's net worth at ~$6.1B (mid-July), with the ~41% DJT stake (~114.75M shares, Trump Media market cap ~$2.5B) and ~$1.424B of crypto-linked lines (~64% of DJT's value); Trump Media launched a paid Wall Street data service tracking Truth Social posts (16 Jul).
superInvestors.deepDive: Disclosed individual buys include NVDA (~$500K, Mar), AAPL (>$650K) and MSFT (>$630K). The crypto exposure and DJT concentration dominate the net-worth picture; the new data-service product and resolved Truth Social legal disputes (20 Jul) are the recent corporate developments.

superInvestors.name: Bridgewater Associates
superInvestors.rationale: No new large 13D/13G or reported Bridgewater move surfaced this run beyond the Q1 book; the fund's diversified, macro-driven positioning is carried pending the 14 Aug Q2 13F.
superInvestors.deepDive: Included for roster completeness; Bridgewater's ETF-heavy, broadly-diversified 13F rarely produces single-name signals. No material change verified this run (gap).

insiders.rationale: Singtel launched a S$2B Value Realisation share buy-back programme (announced 9 Jul), with daily on-market repurchase notices following — a company-level buy signalling management's view that the shares are undervalued. (Corporate action, not individual insider dealing.)
insiders.deepDive: A large, ongoing buyback is a structural bid under one of the portfolio's core SGX blue-chips into the record STI run and the early-August Q2 earnings season. Note: individual SGXNet director/substantial-shareholder interest changes and HKEX disclosures of interest (Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi) did not surface via web search this run and remain unverified GAPS — check links.sgx.com and di.hkex.com.hk directly.

insiders.insider: Ross R. Bhappu (with dir. Bruce D. Hansen)
insiders.rationale: Open-market cluster buying by Energy Fuels’ top brass: CEO Bhappu bought 74,000 shares at $13.08 on 7 Jul (to 256,583 direct) and director Hansen 4,000 at $12.695 on 8 Jul (to 313,844). Both Form 4s accepted by SEC EDGAR 9 Jul 2026.
insiders.deepDive: Rare genuine open-market buys (not option exercises) in the portfolio’s uranium/rare-earth name — management conviction at the $12.70-13.08 zone makes that band an insider-validated reference level. It is also the only confirmed insider BUYING across the portfolio’s mining names this month, against heavy AI-complex insider selling (Arista founder -$54.2M, CoreWeave CEO -$24.8M in 14-16 Jul trades) — a striking sector contrast.

insiders.rationale: Xiaomi repurchased 1.9M Class B shares for HK$50.0M on 22 July 2026 — the most recent tranche in the window — after buying 3.9M shares for HK$100.7M on 15 July (HKEX filings), continuing its multi-tranche buyback program alongside a strong June EV-delivery print (+36% to 34,738 units).
insiders.deepDive: An issuer repurchase signals management's capital-allocation confidence rather than a single insider's personal bet, and Xiaomi's buyback runs in parallel with Tencent's HK program. The near-daily cadence into late July reinforces a company backing its own equity as the EV ramp (YU7 SUV, third straight 30k+ delivery month) diversifies the story beyond handsets/IoT. The corporate bid offers downside support for the holding through tech-sector volatility, though Xiaomi remains a high-beta HK-tech name that swings with the HSTECH tape (and still lags ~-34% YTD, offering relative catch-up if the rally broadens).

insiders.rationale: Tencent repurchased ~1,592,600 shares across 6-9 July 2026 (HK$204.8M on 6 July, HK$12.7M on 8 July and HK$500.7M on 9 July), extending a near-daily buyback streak under the ~912M-share (10%) mandate approved at the 13 May 2026 AGM. Separately, a Tencent unit sold up to ~US$1.55B of Kuaishou in a block trade (filed ~6 July) — a portfolio realization, distinct from the buyback.
insiders.deepDive: Company buybacks are a strong corporate-level conviction signal, and Tencent runs one of the largest repurchase programs in Hong Kong. The relentless daily cadence into July reflects a commitment to shrinking the share count and offsetting dilution from share-based compensation, bullish for holders as the stock coincided with an HK-tech rebound on AI catalysts (HSTECH +300pts, Alibaba ~+11%) and heavy southbound buying into Tencent (+HK$2.32B on 6 July). The parallel Kuaishou block sale is a capital-recycling move, not a signal on Tencent itself. Unlike a director's open-market buy, an issuer repurchase signals management's capital-allocation confidence rather than a single insider's personal bet. As of early July the program had run ~32 consecutive trading days for ~34.5M shares cumulatively under the 13-May mandate (up to ~912M sh / 10%) — a near-mechanical corporate bid underpinning the stock through the HK-tech rebound.

insiders.role: CEO & Executive Director, Mapletree Logistics Trust Mgmt
insiders.rationale: Mapletree Logistics Trust's CEO made an open-market purchase of ~100,000 units at ~S$1.91 in early July 2026, boosting her personal holding by ~73% — a genuine director conviction buy in the S-REIT sleeve as the trust trades near multi-year lows on the higher-for-longer rate backdrop (fresh SGX director-interest change this run).
insiders.deepDive: Unlike an issuer buyback, a CEO's own-account open-market purchase is a direct personal-conviction signal, and a ~73% boost to her stake is meaningful. It lands with MLT under pressure from higher-for-longer rates and a weak logistics-rent cycle in China/HK — the CEO stepping in near the lows is an insider-validated reference level for the industrial-S-REIT complex the book holds (MapletreePACT, Keppel REIT peers). Rate relief from a dovish FOMC pivot is the swing factor; until then the DPU/leverage trajectory caps upside. One of the few fresh, dated SGX director buys verifiable this run against limited SGXNet full-text access.

insiders.rationale: Capital Group crossed above the 5% substantial-shareholder threshold in Singtel, filing a notice showing a total 837,947,249 shares (5.1%) at an average ~S$4.67 — a large institutional accumulation in one of the portfolio's SGX holdings (latest available substantial-shareholder move on the SGX list).
insiders.deepDive: A global institution crossing 5% in Singtel is a meaningful vote of confidence in the telco's ongoing capital-return and asset-recycling story as the STI printed record highs into mid-July. Substantial-shareholder notices are a cleaner institutional signal than director trades and are among the few dated SGX disclosures verifiable this run. The one fresh SGX buyback that surfaced this run was Yangzijiang Maritime Development Ltd — a related but distinct listing from the shipbuilder — repurchasing 1.43M shares for ~S$0.84M across 25-26 June 2026 under an inaugural buyback mandate (recorded here as context; ticker not asserted to avoid mislabeling). No within-window substantial-shareholder or director-interest change was verifiable for DBS, F&N, VICOM, CityDev, UOL, Wing Tai, Yanlord, Ho Bee, Seatrium, CapLandChinaTr, Keppel REIT or Mapletree PACT this run — SGXNet full-text access was limited, so treat that list as unconfirmed rather than empty.

insiders.role: EVP & Chief Sustainability and Development Officer
insiders.rationale: Newmont's EVP sold 3,000 shares (~$277K) at $92.38 on 1 July 2026 (filed 6 July) under a Rule 10b5-1 plan dated 17 December 2025, leaving 43,315 shares — routine, pre-scheduled selling at the world's largest gold miner (a top GDX holding).
insiders.deepDive: This is a scheduled 10b5-1 disposal rather than a discretionary conviction sell, so the signal is muted — executives routinely diversify into strength, and gold near $4,150 makes profit-taking unremarkable. As the largest US-filing gold producer and a core GDX constituent, Newmont insider activity is a useful read on miner sentiment, and the absence of any open-market buying alongside these sales is consistent with a sector that already re-rated hard before June's pullback. Most large GDX/SILJ miners are Canadian foreign private issuers reporting on SEDI rather than US Form 4, so Newmont is one of the few that surfaces in SEC filings.

insiders.rationale: Hecla Mining's General Counsel had ~23,973 shares withheld for tax on RSUs that vested 22 June 2026, with the CFO seeing similar RSU vesting/withholding — equity-compensation events, not open-market buying or selling, at a core silver miner (SILJ/GDX).
insiders.deepDive: These are routine compensation/tax-withholding transactions rather than directional trades, so the signal value is low, but they are among the few recent US Form 4 filings in the largely-Canadian silver-miner universe. Hecla is the largest US primary silver producer and a SILJ constituent, making its filings a window into silver-complex insider behavior that SEDI-reporting peers otherwise hide. No open-market buying accompanied the vesting, consistent with insiders neither chasing nor fading the post-crash silver bounce.

insiders.rationale: Coeur Mining's EVP Exploration made a small open-market purchase of 635 shares (~$10.8K) at $16.95 on 12 June 2026 — the most recent verified Coeur insider transaction, a modest genuine-conviction buy at a US-domiciled silver/gold producer (latest available).
insiders.deepDive: Coeur is one of the few US-domiciled precious-metals miners that files Form 4, making it a window into silver-complex insider sentiment that the largely-Canadian SILJ/SLVP universe hides on SEDI. A small EVP open-market purchase is a modest genuine-conviction buy against a backdrop of plan-based executive selling elsewhere in the sector. With silver whipsawing in the high-$50s to low-$60s, the lack of sizable open-market buying suggests insiders see fair-to-full value rather than a fresh entry point after the multi-quarter run. No newer Coeur Form 4 has surfaced in the past two weeks, so this remains the latest available.

insiders.rationale: DBS CEO Tan Su Shan sold 100,000 shares at S$60.12 on 15 May 2026, leaving ~1.3 million shares (0.048% of the bank), a partial profit-taking trim shortly after the stock first pushed above S$60 — the most recent verified insider move on the SGX-listed holdings (latest available).
insiders.deepDive: The sale came days after DBS reported 1Q2026 net profit of S$2.93 billion (up 1% y/y, 24% q/q) and as the stock hit record territory; DBS has since pushed to a fresh ~S$67 all-time high into its 6 August results. As Singapore's largest lender's first female CEO, Tan retains a sizeable 1.3 million-share holding, so this is a liquidity/diversification trim rather than a loss of confidence. CEO sells into all-time highs are common and often tax-driven, but can cap near-term sentiment given DBS's elevated ~2.2x book valuation and NIM sensitivity to falling SORA. No within-window (24 June-8 July) substantial-shareholder or director-interest change was verifiable for the SGX holdings this run; DBS continues a S$3bn buyback through 2027.
